Tobacco users who die prematurely deprive their families of income, raise the cost of health

heart disease, stroke, and cancer. It exacerbates the problems and complicates the treatments of

other diseases, including diabetes. Money spent on tobacco is money that could have been spent

by households on food and education. Money spent by governments on treating (otherwise

avoidable) tobacco-related diseases is money that could have been spent on roads, education, or

other parts of the health system.
